programme.title: INUYASHIKI LAST HERO [English Subtitle]
programme.desc: Ichiro Inuyashiki is a boring office worker who looks like an old man. Even after building them a new home, his family is nothing but ungrateful. One day, Inuyashiki is diagnosed with terminal cancer. Out on a walk to clear his head, a UFO crashes into him, and his body is rebuilt into a deadly robot. He steps in to stop a group of kids from torturing a homeless man when he is knocked unconscious.

programme.title: INUYASHIKI LAST HERO [English Subtitle]
programme.desc: Reborn a robot, Inuyashiki finds meaning by saving others. Meanwhile, high school student Hiro Shishigami has also been reborn a robot. Shishigami has no regard for anybody aside from his best friend and his family, and uses his robot powers to kill indiscriminately. Contrary to Inuyashiki, he feels alive when he is taking the lives of others. What happens when these two meet?

programme.title: INUYASHIKI LAST HERO [English Subtitle]
programme.desc: Shishigami is rattled to see Inuyashiki stand up from a blow that should have killed him before flying away. programme.title: Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress [English Subtitle]
programme.sub-title: Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress E01 [English Subtitle]
programme.desc: At a time when the industrial revolution was carrying the world into the modern age, a horde of undead monsters suddenly appeared. They could not be killed unless their hearts, which were protected by a layer of iron, were pierced. Humans bitten by them would come back as undead monsters themselves. These undead, which would later be known as "Kabane," exploded in population until they finally overran the world. The people of Hinomoto, a nation in the far east, built fortresses known as "stations" throughout the land that have allowed them to survive the threat of the Kabane. People can only travel between these stations using fortified steam locomotives known as "Hayajiro," and they have managed to stay alive by sharing resources in this way. Ikoma is a young steamsmith living at Aragane Station, a city that specializes in the manufacture of iron and steam engines. He is working on developing a unique anti-Kabane weapon called a "piercing gun" as he waits for his chance to prove his strength. Then, one day, a Hayajiro called the "Iron Fortress" makes its way through the front lines to arrive at Aragane Station. When Ikoma begins his usual maintenance routine, he sees a mysterious girl who is exempt from her Kabane inspection. That night, Ikoma sees the girl again and learns that her name is Mumei, but then an out-of-control Hayajiro overrun by Kabane charges into Aragane Station. The Kabane pour out of the train into Aragane Station. Ikoma races against the flow of the panicked residents, this time determined not to run away, but to defeat the Kabane with his piercing gun!

programme.title: Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress [English Subtitle]
programme.sub-title: Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress E03 [English Subtitle]
programme.desc: At a time when the industrial revolution was carrying the world into the modern age, a horde of undead monsters suddenly appeared. They could not be killed unless their hearts, which were protected by a layer of iron, were pierced. Humans bitten by them would come back as undead monsters themselves. These undead, which would later be known as "Kabane," exploded in population until they finally overran the world. The people of Hinomoto, a nation in the far east, built fortresses known as "stations" throughout the land that have allowed them to survive the threat of the Kabane. People can only travel between these stations using fortified steam locomotives known as "Hayajiro," and they have managed to stay alive by sharing resources in this way. Ikoma is a young steamsmith living at Aragane Station, a city that specializes in the manufacture of iron and steam engines. He is working on developing a unique anti-Kabane weapon called a "piercing gun" as he waits for his chance to prove his strength. Then, one day, a Hayajiro called the "Iron Fortress" makes its way through the front lines to arrive at Aragane Station. When Ikoma begins his usual maintenance routine, he sees a mysterious girl who is exempt from her Kabane inspection. That night, Ikoma sees the girl again and learns that her name is Mumei, but then an out-of-control Hayajiro overrun by Kabane charges into Aragane Station. The Kabane pour out of the train into Aragane Station. Ikoma races against the flow of the panicked residents, this time determined not to run away, but to defeat the Kabane with his piercing gun!

programme.sub-title: Yoshikage Kira Just Wants to Live Quietly, Part 2

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Heart Attack, Part 1

programme.desc: Shinobu tells her husband, Kosaku, that she saw a stray cat in their basement with a hole in its throat. When Kosaku goes down to take a look, he finds the cat already dead, The next morning, a strange plant sprouts from the spot where the cat was buried.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: July 15th (Thurs), Part 1
programme.desc: Yoshihiro Kira spots Kosaku Kawajiri and instantly recognizes that it’s actually his son, Yoshikage. Meanwhile, Josuke, Okuyasu, and Mikitaka find a strange man living in an abandoned electrical tower.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: July 15th (Thurs), Part 2
programme.desc: Josuke enters the electrical tower again to save Mikitaka and defeat Toyohiro Kanedaichi. Meanwhile, Rohan receives a visit from a first-class architect named Masazo Kinoto, who’s come to estimate the repair costs to his burnt house.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: July 15th (Thurs), Part 3
programme.desc: Rohan finds himself possessed by Masazo Kinoto’s Stand, Cheap Trap, who tells the manga artist to burn the photos he took of the people in Morioh. Meanwhile, Josuke and Yuya encounter the Stand user responsible for Koichi’s disappearance.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: July 15th (Thurs), Part 4
programme.desc: Rohan calls over Koichi to help him fight off Cheap Trap, which has attached itself onto Rohan’s back. Unfortunately, Koichi thinks Rohan is pulling a prank on him and leaves.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Bites the Dust, Part 1
programme.desc: Kosaku Kawajiri is forced to kill Hayato after the boy threatens to expose him as a killer. To make matter worse, Kosaku learns from his father, Yoshihiro, that Rohan and the others are coming to investigate the Kawajiri family shortly.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Bites the Dust, Part 2
programme.desc: Yoshikage Kira gains a new ability called Bites the Dust, a bomb that automatically kills anyone who tries to discover Kira’s identity through Hayato. Realizing that the only people who could stop Kira are ones with similar powers.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Shining D (Diamond) is Unbreakable, Part 1
programme.desc: Hayato’s attempt to kill Kira using Stray Cat’s air bullet ends in failure. Kira realizes that letting Hayato repeat the same morning is becoming a risk, so he decides to undo Bites the Dust after he sees through Rohan’s death.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Shining D (Diamond) is Unbreakable, Part 2
programme.desc: Josuke and Hayato hide inside a nearby residence to escape from Deadly Queen and Stray Cat’s attack. But to their horror, Kira is somehow able to close in on them from outside the house.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Goodbye, Morioh – The Heart of Gold
programme.sub-title: Goodbye, Morioh – The Heart of Gold
programme.desc: Josuke and his friends have finally cornered Yoshikage Kira. Refusing to give up, Kira tries to activate Bites the Dust one more time to escape his desperate situation. Can Josuke and the others stop Kira in time to save the future of Morioh?

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Golden Wind
programme.desc: Amid the gritty beauty of Neapolis, the Joestar lineage lives on in Giorno Giovanna. After sidestepping long-term Joestar ally Koichi Hirose, Giorno must contend with two powerful Mafia gangsters, Leaky Eye Lucca and the enigmatic Bruno Bucciarati.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure
programme.desc: Eager to identify Leaky Eye Luca’s attacker, Bucciarati confronts Giorno and unleashes a Stand attack to dismantle him piece by piece. But Giorno counters with his Stand Golden Wind, surprising not just his adversary, but also himself.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Meet the Gangster Behind the Wall
programme.sub-title: Meet the Gangster Behind the Wall
programme.desc: Determined to join the mafia gang Passione, altruistic Giorno is introduced by Bucciarati to the grotesquely corpulent Polpo, an incarcerated capo who tests Giorno’s loyalty with a simple but bizarrely lethal test involving a lighter and its flame.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure
programme.desc: Plodding amid the dusky shadows of a peaceful piazza is Polpo’s macabre Stand, which assails any who dare witness the reigniting of the lighter. Giorno deciphers its method of attack, but is soon staring death in the face as Koichi comes to his aid.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Find Polpo's Fortune!

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure
programme.desc: Sailing to the Isle of Capri to recover Polpo’s estate, Bucciarati and team are ambushed by a stealthy enemy Stand that deflates them into rubber-like human pelts. Abbacchio, however, thinks he can find his comrades and reluctantly activates his Stand.

programme.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure

programme.title: APEC Selfies: Why this ROK entrepreneur wants to call China's shoe capital home
programme.desc: Entrepreneur Michael Lee from ‪the Republic of Korea‬ came to China in 2003. More than two decades later, he now calls Quanzhou in Fujian Province his home. In Jinjiang, a county-level city under Quanzhou and one of China's leading footwear manufacturing hubs, he found a world-class supply chain, constant innovation, and the opportunity to build his own business. His next big plan? To become a true local! #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: Dialogue at the world's largest port: Building resilient port cities together
programme.desc: How can port cities stay resilient amid global trade uncertainty? A sub-forum of the Global Mayors Dialogue in Ningbo was held at the Ningbo Zhoushan Port — the world's No.1 port in cargo throughput for 17 straight years. CGTN's Michael Wang spoke with Ningbo's Vice Mayor and guests from Cotonou (Benin), Klang Royal City (Malaysia) and Toamasina (Madagascar). Arctic shipping routes, green corridors, sister-port cooperation — the insights keep coming!

programme.title: Smart governance, shared future: How innovation is changing our cities
programme.desc: Robots that write, grasp objects and work on real production lines are becoming an everyday reality in Ningbo. How is innovation transforming our cities? From humanoid robots and smart urban governance to balancing tourism in Florence and developing a digital city atlas in Egypt, the future is already here. Learn more at this sub-forum of the Global Mayors Dialogue in #Ningbo. #Zhejiang

programme.title: Live: Could China be the birthplace of the next global unicorn?
programme.desc: At this year's China International Import Expo (CIIE), the Innovation Incubation Special Section spotlights promising startups, showcasing breakthroughs in AI, robotics, green technology, digital health, and advanced manufacturing. Under the theme "In China, Dive into New Arenas," the one-stop platform connects global startups with investors, industry leaders, and more. It also serves as a window into the upcoming APEC. Which emerging technologies could shape our future? And could the next unicorn be born here? Join CGTN's Zhu Tianlu to find out.

programme.title: How can AI and robots transform the way we receive healthcare?
programme.desc: From cutting-edge medical devices and AI-powered healthcare solutions to surgical robots changing the operating room, the latest innovations are reshaping the future of medicine at the Medical Equipment & Healthcare Products Exhibition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE). Can robots make surgery smarter and more precise? How is AI changing healthcare? Join CGTN's Bi Ran and Cao Chufeng as they explore the technologies transforming medical care.

programme.title: China's ocean economy at a turning point
programme.desc: Since elevating the goal of becoming a "maritime power" in 2012, China has made significant progress. What are the most eye-catching achievements? As the focus shifts from speed to quality, how could China's AI and digital tech edge help reshape the country's traditional maritime sectors? And in a system where a few countries still hold technological and narrative dominance, how can China gain a greater voice in rule-setting through global cooperation? Host TU Yun joins Yan Yan, a senior research fellow with the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, Qu Qiang, a professor and fellow of the Belt and Road Research Center at Minzu University of China, and Warwick Powell, an adjunct professor at Queensland University of Technology, to navigate the opportunities, challenges, and what lies beneath the surface.

programme.title: How China's ocean kingdom makes billions
programme.desc: In Southern China, a theme park you've likely never heard of is attracting more annual visitors than Hollywood Universal. The question is, how? Meet Chimelong Ocean Kingdom. It holds seven Guinness World Records and features the largest aquarium on earth. CGTN's Yu Hongyu dives into the strategy behind the splash to see how a local park created a hundred-billion-dollar opportunity.

programme.title: China's Kungfu theme park: A wild ride back in time
programme.desc: At Wansuishan Martial Arts City in central China’s Kaifeng, Henan Province, you’re not just a visitor - you’re part of the story. Every segment in the park is part of an immersive experience rooted in Chinese martial arts and traditional culture. From live matchmaking shows to iron flower performances, from Song Dynasty streets to interactive stages, this uniquely Chinese theme park – with not even one roller coaster or scary ride – was able to record over 24 million visits in 2025.

programme.title: Bizfocus: From myth to reality: How tech brings Eastern imagination to life
programme.desc: Ever wondered what China’s version of “Adam and Eve” or “Beauty and the Beast” looks like? While the world’s theme parks are all about Western fairy tales, one Chinese park took a different path—Fantawild brings ancient Eastern myths to life with mind-blowing tech and art. In this episode of Bizfocus, CGTN’s Xu Yi and her new friends from Pakistan and Bangladesh go for adventure in Fantawild Oriental Heritage in Mianyang, Sichuan. Gods, legends, and the tech behind the magic—all in one epic trip.

programme.title: Biztalk Special Coverage on AI EP3
programme.desc: The Token Economy Demand for AI tokens is surging, with trends like “tokenmaxxing” accelerating the race for computing power. As pressure mounts on computing and energy infrastructure, China is leveraging its clean energy strengths to support AI growth, while “token exports” emerge as a new way to deliver AI services to global users. What’s the future like for the “token economy”? Join us on BizTalk as we explore the economics behind the AI revolution.

programme.title: COP31: From pledges to action
programme.desc: As COP31 unfolds in Türkiye, global climate action faces mounting political and economic challenges. With some major economies scaling back climate commitments and competition for green technologies intensifying, can the world turn climate pledges into action? What role can China play? Join CGTN BizTalk as leading climate experts examine the challenges facing COP31, the future of green industries, and the shifting dynamics of global climate cooperation.

programme.title: China-US partnerships fueling rapid growth
programme.desc: Starbucks landed in China when coffee was a novelty. Today, 1 in 5 stores globally is there. American fast food and retail giants placed the same bet, and cashed in. Now local brands are out-executing them. The fix? Partner with Chinese private equity. Here's why it's working, and what it means for both sides.

programme.title: The green bridge between China & US
programme.desc: In 2019, Tesla was running on fumes. Shanghai handed it a lifeline, a gigafactory built in 10 months. Today, that plant produces nearly half of all Teslas using 95% local parts. That same playbook is expanding across green tech, pairing Chinese battery tech with American software. When the world's two largest economies build together, clean energy gets cheaper and faster for everyone.

programme.title: China-US: The efficiency advantage
programme.desc: The iPhone in your pocket? A global masterpiece. Apple's supply chain spans the world, with America's design expertise meeting China's manufacturing strength. Precision, speed and scale turn bold ideas into products in your hands. And this goes beyond Apple: cooperation across borders can drive innovation and growth. When the world's two biggest economies click, everyone benefits.

programme.title: RAZOR: Ghost Ponds
programme.desc: Europe has lost at least 50 percent of its ponds over the last century. Many have been filled in to make room for new developments, or drained to expand farmland. Ponds may seem like a small part of the environmental landscape, but are actually crucial to biodiversity and the fight against climate change. RAZOR's Reya El-Salahi meets Professor Carl Sayer and Dr Helen Greaves from the Norfolk Ponds Project, who are on a mission to restore ponds in the UK and spark an environmental restoration. As part of an initiative backed by University College London and an EU-funded consortium called the Ponderful project, they lead expeditions to the county of Norfolk, where they aim to restore two kinds of ponds: "ghost ponds", that have either been drained or filled, and "zombie ponds" that are too overgrown and not functioning as well as they can.

programme.title: RAZOR Conversations: Sandra Diaz
programme.desc: The greatest threat facing humanity may not be climate change, but the collapse of biodiversity. The fabric of life itself, plants, animals, soils, water and ecosystems, underpins everything from the food we eat to the air we breathe. Yet that fabric is fraying at an alarming rate. Sandra Díaz, a Professor at Oxford University, is one of the world's leading ecologists and one of the most influential voices in global environmental science. An advisor to the United Nations and a key figure in international biodiversity policy, Díaz argues that biodiversity loss is not a separate environmental issue but a crisis that strikes at the foundations of human life. The damage we do to nature, she says, is ultimately damage we do to ourselves. In this episode of RAZOR: Conversations, Reya El-Salahi speaks with Díaz about why biodiversity should not be seen as something distant, confined to rainforests or endangered species, but as something intimately connected to our daily lives, economies, cultures and futures.

programme.title: BizPodcast: Why are global entrepreneurs choosing Shenzhen?
programme.desc: What makes Shenzhen such an attractive place to launch a business? With the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting approaching, all eyes are on this innovation-driven city in China. But beyond its reputation as a tech hub, what does it actually take to turn a big idea into a real product here? In this episode of #BizPodcast, CGTN talks with two entrepreneurs about why they chose Shenzhen, how they bring ideas to market, and what young founders should know before starting a business. Would you consider starting a business in Shenzhen? What would you want to know first?

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: How to build a digital twin of a city？
programme.desc: As cities expand and grow more intricate, a new kind of specialist is emerging behind the scenes: the urban digital twin engineer. In the coastal city of Qingdao, these experts are using real-time data and AI to build virtual replicas of the city—helping predict risks, improve infrastructure, and protect the public. CGTN's Liu Jiaxin takes us inside this fast-growing field.

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: From trash to treasure
programme.desc: Jiao Jianwei is a senior engineer at the Longgang Energy Eco-Park inShenzhen. Every day, the facility processes 5,000 tonnes of waste, burning it togenerate electricity that powers millions of homes. The leftover ash is alsoturned into eco-bricks, used to pave city roads. From landfills to incineration,China has transformed its waste industry with advanced technologies. Today,the country operates more than 1,000 waste-to-energy plants – nearly half theworld's total. With national goals like "carbon neutrality" and "zero-wastecities" taking shape, engineers like Jiao are turning trash into treasure.

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: Who runs China's sea-roving protein factory?
programme.desc: Ever seen "fishermen" farming salmon on a vessel with a displacement bigger than some aircraft carriers? On China's Suhai-1 – the world's first deep-sea salmon and trout aquaculture vessel – these cold-water, high-latitude fish are now thriving far from their natural habitat.

programme.title: China's concert boom: Why Gen Z is filling the stadiums
programme.desc: From packed stadium shows to sold-out performances in smaller cities, China's live music scene is expanding rapidly. programme.title: The self-care economy explained: How emotional spending is reshaping consumer trends
programme.desc: For months, Chinese social feeds have been filled with "Lao Ji"- a third-person way of saying "me." What began as a slang sign-off, "Love you, Lao Ji. See you tomorrow," now signals a broader shift toward self-care and emotional self-support. It also feeds a huge market where young consumers are rechanneling budgets toward small, meaningful purchases that support emotional wellbeing. In this episode of Unboxing China, we trace how a casual phrase turned into a cultural movement, reshaping consumption and mental-health talk.

programme.title: Fearless Journey Ep.8
programme.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-2 Chinese Wrestling
programme.desc: In Episode 2, Chinese Wrestling, host Kleber joins a public training session led by Wang Tongqing, a master preserving the imperial Shanpu Ying wrestling tradition. Swept up in the group's lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master's skill. Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang's story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge between history and the present.

programme.title: Guqin Music Art
programme.desc: Almost unchanged in its 3,000-year history, the guqin and its music gained UNESCO recognition in 2003. This episode of The Inheritors explores the past, present and future of his timeless art form.

programme.title: China IRL: Beijing Riverside
programme.desc: Three long-term China residents swap traditional tourism for real life, exploring culture and trends in Travelogue's new series. In this episode they check out the river swimming, fishing, and leisure scene at Beijing's Liangma River, before heading to Tuanjiehu Park for pull-ups, Tai Chi, and visions of a Beijing retirement.

programme.title: Aerial China III Ep.8
programme.desc: Hunan, in south-central China, is cradled by mountains on three sides. With rolling hills and cross-crossing rivers flowing into Dongting Lake and the Yangtze, this is a land that has given breath to a culture of diligence and endeavor that has expressed itself as eloquently on the province's fields and terraces as it has in the books produced by its many scholars and poets...

programme.title: A Bite of China IV Ep.1
programme.desc: The fourth series of ‘A Bite of China’ takes a deep dive into seven often-overlooked culinary realms: handcrafted street snacks, local eateries, county flavors, food markets, farms, kitchens and restaurants. In short, it’s a documentary series that makes an invaluable contribution to the chronicling of China’s collective food memory.

programme.title: Gourmets Alive Ep.8
programme.desc: What did China's most celebrated scholars and poets eat? This documentary follows the trail of famous cultural figures from ancient to modern times, using reenactments to explore the classic dishes that helped define China’s rich culinary history.

programme.title: Foodwise: Kunming
programme.desc: Join host Tianran He in Kunming, the capital of Yunnan province in southwest China. Named the Spring City for its perennially good weather, Kunming is one of China's most ethnically diverse cities, something that's reflected in its food: From boozy sticky rice for breakfast, to the famous "Crossing the Bridge" rice noodles, and evening barbecues, there's plenty on offer here. Also, it's mushroom season, and Tianran is taking to the hills to hunt for wild fungi - but he'll need a trusty friend to steer him away from the poisonous ones!

programme.title: Foodwise: Shaoxing
programme.desc: Join host Tianran He in the historic water town of Shaoxing, famed for its yellow wine. Traversing its canals by boat, Tianran discovers why it's said there are 10,000 bridges in Shaoxing, before enjoying the freshest catch of the day. But as it turns out, Shaoxing's climate is also perfect for fermentation, leading to a wide array of unique local foods that can sometimes be both smelly and delicious - and at other times, downright unforgettable!

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the "Roof of the World" in China's southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. Finally, Tianran dons his apron and learns to make iconic Tibetan dishes, including one said to reveal your fortune!

programme.desc: What did China's most celebrated scholars and poets eat? This documentary follows the trail of famous cultural figures from ancient to modern times, using reenactments to explore the classic dishes that helped define China’s rich culinary history.

programme.title: Foodwise: Haikou
programme.desc: Welcome to Haikou, also known as the Coconut City! Join Tianran He in experiencing the unique culinary culture and urban character of this tropical paradise. From light and sweet coconut chicken hotpot to refreshing herbal desserts and spicy rice soup - a local favourite, every bite tells the story of the city's laid-back charm and beauty. We'll explore everything from Haikou's winding alleys and mangrove forests, to the culture of its southeast Asian diaspora, so come and discover this magical destination with us.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hainan's Four Famous Dishes
programme.desc: The stunning east coast of Hainan in southeast China, attract numerous visitors to travel. The reason that people tend to visit Hianan not only because of the beautiful beach view but also delicious local cuisine in Hainan. Hainan's four famous dishes is Chicken, duck, goat and crab. In Wenchang, the ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, people could discover the original version of Hainan Chicken Rice and see how local chickens free range on coconut meat. In Qionghai, seat of the Boao Forum for Asia, you may dine on duck and goat, before feasting on crab in the surfer haven of Wanning.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.2
programme.desc: Tianran He explores Lhasa's bustling Barkhor Street, where pilgrims, locals, and visitors alike circle its ancient lanes. This multicultural district, home to sacred temples and boutique shops, becomes the backdrop as Tianran dons traditional Tibetan attire for a photoshoot. Across the city, he meets high school students dancing for Douyin - China's version of TikTok, blending street dance with traditional Tibetan moves. Finally, Tianran travels to the birthplace of Tibetan incense, where waterwheels still power this thousand-year-old craft.

programme.title: Fearless Journey Ep.9
programme.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-3 Shaolin Style
programme.desc: Episode 3, Shaolin, explores how this thousand-year-old temple has evolved into a unique "kung fu platform" that draws enthusiasts from around the world. Host Kleber immerses himself in Shaolin's integrated way of life, where Chan (Zen) practice and martial training go hand in hand, and turns the camera toward foreign practitioners pursuing their kung fu dreams both inside and beyond the temple gates. Along the way, he meets international disciples living and training at Shaolin, as well as students learning the rare art of Shaolin Xinyiba under Master Hu Zhengsheng, a former Shaolin monk. At martial arts schools near Songshan Mountain, Kleber also encounters overseas competitors training hard for the arena. Together, their stories reveal Shaolin kung fu's enduring pull, one that crosses cultures and borders while uniting practitioners through tradition, discipline, and self-mastery.

programme.title: Peking Opera
programme.desc: Delving into the world of Peking Opera, this episode of Inheritors features renowned masters of the art, to learn about this treasured art from behind the scenes. We also visit the Beijing Guoyi Children's Peking Opera Troupe to see how Peking Opera shapes the lives of young students.

programme.title: China IRL: Beijing Hutongs
programme.desc: Jack, Alex and Tianran wander Beijing's historic laneways, taking in traditional sweets, historical views, and a centuries-old kite-making tradition. Reflecting on the coexistence of ancient customs and hyper-modern life, they climb Beihai Park's iconic white stupa to enjoy an "emperor's view" below.

programme.title: Aerial China III Ep.9
programme.desc: Hebei is, in a sense, a sort of geographic compendium of the whole of China. With the Yan Mountains demarcate plateaus from plains, they also stand guard over the strategic corridor linking the northeast to the country's heartland.

programme.title: Dream Builders: Stories from China and Europe
programme.desc: On the occasion of the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and the EU, Inheritors of China launches a special multimedia series titled "Dream Builders: Stories from China and Europe." Taking culture as the starting point, the series responds to public discourse by telling the real-life stories of Europeans living in China. programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: In this episode of Aging in the Wild, we explore the physiological secrets and factors that determine life expectancy in various animal species. From the seventy-year-old elephant to the quasi-immortal hydra, and the more than a hundred-year-old tortoise, we explore life expectancy, longevity and senescence. Can we distinguish between the effects of the environment and the internal adaptations that lead to longevity? What are some of the benefits associated with aging in nature?

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Reproduction is not only a concern of the young and restless: this episode of Aging in the Wild brings a light-hearted look at the issue of sexuality and camaraderie in older animals. We illustrate, for example, the link between the age of an elephant and its reproductive success. What are the reproductive benefits of these animals as they grow older? Through hearing their stories, we learn of some of the advantages - and disadvantages - of late-life reproduction.

programme.title: To The Ends Of The Earth
programme.desc: The rise of extreme energy, the end of economic growth, the people caught in the middle. To the Ends of the Earth is a feature documentary about the state of our energy system today, and the people we meet are uniquely positioned to watch this global crossroads unfold. For example, the mayor of an Inuit village in Canada's high Arctic who is concerned that seismic testing for oil in the ocean is blowing up the eardrums of the animals that the Inuit hunt to survive. Or the environmental lawyer who goes on a journey to areas that produce energy for the Tarsands of Alberta – he learns of the inputs of energy that have to be put into this resource - and the reasons why the second largest oil project in the world is economically unsustainable. Or the river conservationist in Utah who fights to protect the Colorado River from oil shale projects that would disturb its headwaters.

programme.title: Kanga Pan: An African Horror Story
programme.desc: Kanga Pan – An African Horror Story is a spine-chilling, one-off wildlife documentary, the first of its kind. A relatively unknown inland waterhole in Mana Pools National Park, Kanga Pan is a gathering point for a melting pot of wildlife species. On the surface, it looks like a peaceful oasis, offering the cooling refreshment of water and bathing.

programme.title: Sharks: The Big Five
programme.desc: The ocean has its own Big Five. Featuring great whites, to hammerheads, tigers, bulls, and the intimidating whale shark, this is the ultimate shark show. Delve deep into the African waters and discover a new side of these prehistoric predators of the sea, while reconsidering the Hollywood portrayal which has done much to damage the reputation of these gentle creatures.

programme.title: Africa: The Serengeti
programme.desc: Chronicles a spectacle that few humans have ever witnessed, the Great Migration, taking viewers on a journey with over 1.5 million animals as they travel more than 500 miles across the Serengeti plains in Tanzania and Kenya.

programme.title: Strange Creatures of the Batangas Sea
programme.desc: Hidden in the magical underwater world of one of the most biodiverse marine areas on the planet exists a community of spectacular animals more peculiar than we can imagine.

programme.title: The Best of Worlds: Life at Its Alpine Limits
programme.desc: For 5000 years man has sought to inhabit the more accessible areas of Europe, but at its very heart, in the high zones of the Alps, there exists a world parallel to ours.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: As the woods prepare to sleep and mushrooms grow as the first rains fall, flocks of cranes migrate home to Spain from their summer season in the north. The stags clash their antlers in pursuit of the does; there is little time before winter sets in.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: The unknown face of Spain. Snow, rain, clouds, and cold envelop the land. The ibex migrate to the valleys, and wolves patrol the mountains as vultures circle the skies overhead. Though the landscape looks bleak and barren at a glance, there is life thriving here.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: The sun heats the Earth, and life begins again. As they prepare to breed, animals wake from hibernation and build nests in treetops and caves. Whether reptiles, birds, or mammals, all the spring babies fight for survival through their first, most challenging days.

programme.title: Life On Fire
programme.desc: Nicaragua, in the middle of Central America, is home to Masaya; a huge volcano that has been active for over 30,000 years. During its long life it has caused some of the largest eruptions in history. The surrounding landscape has been created from lava, ash and gas while at the centre lies a desolate, empty land. Each time the Masaya volcano destroys everything around it, life returns, re-emerging from the ash at its fee

programme.title: Life On Fire
programme.desc: In the vast emptiness of the Pacific Ocean, tectonic movements construct or destroy islands. In the Tongan archipelago, two little-known animals have learnt to cope with these ephemeral lands: the sooty tern, a seabird that never dares wet its wings for fear of drowning and the Alvin shrimp, a blind crustacean that nonetheless manages to find its way around the abyss. When an underwater volcano becomes an island, the fates of these two living paradoxes are linked.

programme.title: Life On Fire
programme.desc: In 2010, the eruption of the Eyjafjallajokull volcano in Iceland provoked a vast economic chaos by paralysing one of the world's major air traffic networks for several days. Through spectacular aerial footage, the film tries to understand which volcano could wake up next and what the consequences of a major eruption are likely to be. The world has come to realize that a colossal power sleeps beneath Iceland but Icelanders have learned to live amongst their volcanoes for centuries.

programme.title: Anaconda - The Silent Killer
programme.desc: Few snakes are feared more and understood less than the anaconda. The film shows the journey into remote and uncharted parts of the Amazon rainforest to find the truth behind the mythical beast. Lush green forests abound with colorful toucans, noisy howler monkeys, strange tapirs, and vibrant Amazon Indian tribes. But hiding in the dense vegetation and murky swamps is also the biggest and most powerful snake in the world: the anaconda.

programme.title: Leopard Seals, Lords of the Ice
programme.desc: Göran Ehlmé, a naturalist and specialist in cold water diving, is haunted by the memory of a terrible encounter with a still unknown predator, a seal that looks like an ogre: the sea leopard. A giant seal that lives on the edge of the planet in the most inhospitable place there is: Antarctica, a world of ice and rock. Göran sets out to meet this super predator to unlock some of its secrets. He witnesses a dramatic face-to-face encounter between several leopard seals and a colony of penguins, a unique opportunity to see and film unprecedented hunting behaviour.

programme.title: Roaring With Pride
programme.desc: Penya and Paza encounter a python; the adorable cubs go on their first bush outing; Lewa and Laili keep the zebra on their toes. Meanwhile, the research team have more experiments for the Ngamo lions.

programme.title: Roaring With Pride
programme.desc: The lions are on the hunt for giraffe. Meanwhile, researcher Rae accompanies the lions as they encounter nervy hartebeest. The game capture unit are tasked with supplying more zebra for the Ngama release site. And don’t miss the action as hungry Kwali zones in on an unsuspecting zebra. But can she hold on?

programme.title: Turtle Odyssey
programme.desc: Sea turtles are some of Earth's most ancient and majestic creatures. For over 100 million years, they have traversed the seas, enduring mass extinctions and playing critical roles in maintaining food webs. But now they face a new threat – humans. It's time we learned more about these remarkable reptiles.

programme.title: Pharm to Table
programme.desc: How far would you go, to know what's in your food? As we go about our daily lives, few of us stop to wonder what our food is really made of. Taylor Lancastor travels 2800 miles on foot, to defend our right to know, and discover the truth of what we are being fed.

programme.title: Secret Seychelles: D’Arros
programme.desc: D'Arros is one of the Seychelles' best kept secrets. Safe-guarded by isolation, the island is a jewel of the Indian Ocean. Teaming with wildlife, the sand cay and neighbouring coral atoll are home to rare giant tortoises, hawksbill turtles, and shearwaters. In the depths, dolphins, greater hammerhead and tiger sharks roam. Green turtles nest on the pristine beaches, reef sharks bear live pups in the shallow lagoon, whales come to the deep channel, and mantas feed over coral reefs. Now designated as a wildlife reserve this natural treasure trove has the recognition it so rightly deserves.

programme.title: Japan: The Sense of Season
programme.desc: In this episode, we delve into the spring and summer months. Spring is a time of fleeting beauty as Japan’s famous cherry blossom drifts across the nation and wild visitors welcome the warming conditions. As spring rolls into summer, dramatic festivals, mysterious animals and seasonal harvests spark into life right across Japan’s islands and coastal waters.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Observing two massive elk clashing their antlers is to witness a true demonstration of power. For other species, such as the European marmot, remaining in power is a matter of collaborating with family and community. Are these animals forced to give up their hard-won social status as they age? Through this lens, we take a deep and entertaining look at the challenges faced by those in power ... and what it takes to stay there.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: In many human cultures, elders play a vital role in the well-being of communities and are responsible for passing down knowledge and culture. Is it any wonder to find that the orca, the elephant, and the wolf, have been found to transmit their respective cultures to the younger generations? Young animals learn by observing their elders. Judging when to fight or take flight, deciding how to choose a life partner, learning where to find food, these are just some of the skills passed down through the generations as elders share their wisdom.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore how different animal species react to impending death. We explore the factors that lead animals to their final resting places: disease, injury, predation, drought, famine. Some species, such as the naked mole rat, while not immortal, seem to be able to effectively protect themselves from certain diseases such as cancer. This raises questions about what is no doubt a sensitive subject, one that brings to mind our own mortality as we speculate about the reasons for this kind of resilience in our animal counterparts. What lessons can we learn from the animal kingdom? We follow individuals to their last breath ... not as voyeurs, but as spectators attuned to the circle of life.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore how different animal species react to impending death. We explore the factors that lead animals to their final resting places: disease, injury, predation, drought, famine. Some species, such as the naked mole rat, while not immortal, seem to be able to effectively protect themselves from certain diseases such as cancer. This raises questions about what is no doubt a sensitive subject, one that brings to mind our own mortality as we speculate about the reasons for this kind of resilience in our animal counterparts. What lessons can we learn from the animal kingdom? We follow individuals to their last breath ... not as voyeurs, but as spectators attuned to the circle of life.

programme.title: Serengeti: Journey to the Heart of Africa
programme.desc: Life happened in the Serengeti on an unprecedented scale. It's home to most of Africa's most iconic animals, and hosts one of the world's greatest natural events — the annual wildebeest migration. Nature has orchestrated a perfect symphony in which every species has a very distinct role to play in a larger story -- the balance of an entire ecosystem. We'll see it through the eyes of the youngest members of our animal cast as they imitate their parents, and learn about the mighty roles they'll play. Prepare to be awed by this immersive Giant Screen film about how nature works in one of the world's greatest ecosystems.

programme.title: Serengeti: Journey to the Heart of Africa
programme.desc: Life happened in the Serengeti on an unprecedented scale. It's home to most of Africa's most iconic animals, and hosts one of the world's greatest natural events — the annual wildebeest migration. Nature has orchestrated a perfect symphony in which every species has a very distinct role to play in a larger story -- the balance of an entire ecosystem. We'll see it through the eyes of the youngest members of our animal cast as they imitate their parents, and learn about the mighty roles they'll play. Prepare to be awed by this immersive Giant Screen film about how nature works in one of the world's greatest ecosystems.

programme.title: The Ultimate Wave Tahiti
programme.desc: The Ultimate Wave Tahiti follows eleven-time World Champion surfer Kelly Slater and Tahitian surfer Raimana Van Bastolear as they explore the nature of waves and hunt for the ultimate wave-riding experience at the famed Pacific surf site of Teahupoo, Tahiti.

programme.title: Giant Sea Serpent: Meet the Myth
programme.desc: Its 10-meter length and silver ribbon shape inspired the myth of the sea serpent. Off the French Riviera, buoys set 2,000 meters deep attract pelagic species, including the Giant Oarfish—“King of Herrings”—drifting vertically, alone or in pairs. With expert guidance and passionate collaborators, a scientific expedition unveils the biology of this mysterious ambassador of the abyss.

programme.title: A Volcano Odyssey
programme.desc: Follow the story of 65 millions years of evolution around a volcanic hotspot in the Indian Ocean. Discover how a lava gush flooded an area as large as France, partially caused the demise of dinosaurs but also helped the emergence of mammals and new life forms.

programme.title: Last Devils
programme.desc: Tasmanian Devils are the world's largest carnivorous marsupials and they are only found in Tasmania. Through hundreds of hours of filming in the wild, we reveal how fights over food are a carefully choreographed ritual, we witness the seemingly brutal mating process, see tiny young developing inside their mother's pouch, and visit wild devil pups play-fighting and hunting as they prepare for life in the outside world.

programme.title: The Rhino Orphanage: Lesedi
programme.desc: The Rhino Orphanage receives a call for help, a calf was stuck in mud for three days, abandoned and unable to walk. Then Karen rushes to a rhino that may need to be euthanized and is possibly pregnant! Horrors of the poaching war are revealed at an incident close to the Kruger National Park.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: These are the days of thirst: it is hot. Only the mountains are cool; everywhere else suffers in heat between 40 and 50°C. The rain is long forgotten. Each day is a search for shade and water. Amphibians bury themselves in mud to escape dehydration. The rest of the wild must wait for the cool of the night to move.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: As the woods prepare to sleep and mushrooms grow as the first rains fall, flocks of cranes migrate home to Spain from their summer season in the north. The stags clash their antlers in pursuit of the does; there is little time before winter sets in.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: The unknown face of Spain. Snow, rain, clouds, and cold envelop the land. The ibex migrate to the valleys, and wolves patrol the mountains as vultures circle the skies overhead. Though the landscape looks bleak and barren at a glance, there is life thriving here.

programme.title: Hurricanes: Rise of the Superstorms
programme.desc: Hurricanes are the strongest storms on earth. They can inflict losses of billions of dollars and thousands of lives. Beyond the hype that surrounds these dangerous events, are stories of significance to society, nature and the future. Collaboration with world-class scientists sheds new light on this lethal phenomenon.

programme.title: Mike O'Meara - Predicting the Unpredictable
programme.desc: Episode one explores the search for Hurricane scientists “holy grail” seeking to understand the dangerous increases in storm power called rapid intensification.

programme.title: Mike O'Meara - Shaping the Wilderness
programme.desc: This episode looks at varying strategies used by plants and animals that live in the hurricane zone and how they cope with the annual onslaught.

programme.title: Mike O'Meara - Winds of Change
programme.desc: For millennia, hurricanes have threatened the Eastern USA, the Caribbean and parts of Latin America. But changes to global climate have serious consequences for the future.

programme.title: Adventure Ocean Quest: The Great White Sharks of Guadalupe
programme.desc: The great white shark has a fearsome reputation and diving with them is definitely a risky business. But Frederic wants to show a different side of the infamous great white: Mexican zoologist Mauricio Hoyos believes that their aggression is triggered by excessive disturbance in the water. He wants to get to the bottom of the sharks' secretive migrations and their interactions with other species, including humans.

programme.title: Predator's Playground
programme.desc: This African spring is a lifeline and a trap. Flowing from a sandy riverbed 30 km from the Zambezi, it draws animals from August to November. But cliffs turn it into an ambush zone for lion prides, who strike with deadly precision, taking prey from buffalo to baby elephants. It’s a predator’s playground.

programme.title: Great Species of Africa - Wildebeest
programme.desc: Witness nature’s greatest spectacle, the annual wildebeest migration, where over one and a half million wildebeest follow an ancient pattern driven by rainfall and fertile soils.

programme.title: Great Species of Africa - Vultures
programme.desc: Learn just why we cannot afford to have a Savanna without vultures. These birds are known as the great recyclers of the Savanna – and it’s the intensity with which they do their jobs that sometimes get them a bad rap – when in fact they rarely, if ever, kill anything themselves.

programme.title: Great Species of Africa - Elephants
programme.desc: Travel alongside a herd of elephants and see the amazing journey of these majestic creatures, who can travel up to 100 miles in a day, following ancient routes remembered by the Matriarch and passed on for generations.

programme.title: Great Species of Africa - Hyenas
programme.desc: Discover much more than meets the eye about hyenas, bold and curious animals that show intellect unlike any other animal on the Savanna.

programme.title: When Shark Meets Croc
programme.desc: The most aggressive of ocean predators, the bull shark, is notorious for leaving the safety of the deep blue ocean, venturing far up the murky rivers of Africa's coast in search of prey. But lurking in these shadowy places is Africa's deadliest killer - the Nile crocodile. Reports of clashes between the two are many but marine researchers Ryan Johnson and Tess Hempson, are determined to find out the truth.

programme.title: Inhabit: A permaculture Perspective
programme.desc: Inhabit: A Permaculture Perspective explores the many environmental issues facing us today and examines solutions that are being applied using the ecological design process called "permaculture"; a design method and philosophy of life with great potential for solving issues related to agriculture, economics and governance. 'Inhabit' provides an intimate look at permaculture peoples and practices ranging from rural, suburban and urban landscapes. This beautifully made documentary presents a vast array of projects, concepts and translates the diversity of permaculture into something that can be understood by an equally diverse audience. For those familiar, it will be a call to action and a glimpse into what's possible. For those unfamiliar, it will be an introduction to a new way of being and a new way of relating to the Earth. For everyone, it will be a reminder that humans are capable of being planetary healing forces. Audience Favorite Princeton Environmental Film Festival 2015. Audience Choice Award EFFY Environmental Film Festival Yale 2015. Official Selections 2015: Food + Farm Film Fest SF, G2 Green Earth Film Festival, FICMA, Life Sciences Film Festival Prague, American Conservation Film Festival, Finger Lakes Environmental Film Festival, ITSA Back to Nature Film Festival & Crossroads Festival for Documentary Film and Discourse.

programme.title: Strange Creatures of the Batangas Sea
programme.desc: Hidden in the magical underwater world of one of the most biodiverse marine areas on the planet exists a community of spectacular animals more peculiar than we can imagine.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Baja-Revillagigedo
programme.desc: In the Pacific Ocean, south of the Tropic of Cancer and the Mexican state of Baja California Sur, lie the small islands of Revillagigedo. The marine area proves to be exceptional, as being a protected area in the middle of the Pacific Ocean has allowed the species to proliferate and prosper.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Aqaba
programme.desc: North of the Red Sea, at the perfect crossroads linking three continents – Asia, Africa and Europe – lies Aqaba. The 1000 fish and 200 coral species that live in its coastal waters make the city an ideal place for environmentalists and marine biologists.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Anilao
programme.desc: If anything stands out in the Filipino town of Anilao, it is the reefs, declared a World Heritage Site by the UNESCO. In fact, the Philippines are the part of the Coral Triangle with the greatest marine biodiversity.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Seychelles
programme.desc: Seychelles is located in the Indian Ocean, northeast of Madagascar and east of Somalia, Kenya, and Tanzania. Its turquoise waters hide more than 1000 fish species, making it a prime destination for diving.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Brazil
programme.desc: Brazil's Pernambuco state is home to the national marine park where gardnes of colored corals, big marine animals and amazing wrecks contribute to the splendor of this place.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Southern Red Sea
programme.desc: Egypt is one of the best connected countries in the Middle East and the Red Sea is called the aquarium of the world. Million colours and species fill its waters and makes it a great diving destination.

programme.desc: Professionele atleten gebruiken muziek om zich op te peppen voor een grote wedstrijd, maar waarom kan muziek ons inspireren, motiveren en aan het huilen maken?

programme.title: Bright Now S1
programme.desc: Zonnezeilen, het nieuwste op het gebied van ruimtevaarttechnologie, zouden ons op een dag kunnen helpen om nabije sterren te bereiken. Kijk mee met de spannende missies die de basis leggen voor een nieuwe vorm van ruimteverkenning.

programme.title: Bright Now S1
programme.desc: Casey Anderson groeide op in Montana en begon al op jonge leeftijd van wilde dieren te houden en ze te waarderen. Hij vond een bijzondere verwantschap met beren. Op een dag stond hij voor een noodlottige beslissing: een verweesd grizzlywelpje in het wild te laten sterven of te redden.

programme.title: Bright Now S1

programme.title: Ghost Chasers S1
programme.desc: Kay en het team onderzoeken paranormale activiteit in een van de spookachtigste steden van België, Namen, waar het team ervan overtuigd is dat het door een geest wordt gevolgd.

programme.title: Power & S3
programme.desc: Amit Himelstein is hoofdinstructeur van de IKG en leider in Kapap. Zijn grote motto? Iedereen respecteren, maar voor niemand bang zijn. Hij is de ware belichaming van krav maga.

programme.title: Power & S3
programme.desc: Denise Kielholz is zesvoudig wereldkampioen kickboxen. Haar doel? 's Werelds eerste vrouwelijke MMA-wereldkampioen worden, en ze doet alles om dat doel te behalen.

programme.title: Power & S3
programme.desc: Dave Leduc is de ongeslagen wereldkampioen Lethwei, de hardste sport ter wereld. Deze wordt gevochten zonder handschoenen, maar met ellebogen, kopstoten en door de ander neer te halen.

programme.title: Breaking Limits S1
programme.desc: Speed skater Beorn Nijenhuis en presentator Julien Chang bezoeken laboratoria om te vragen hoe technologie helpt het verschil te maken tussen zilver en goud.

programme.title: Breaking Limits S1
programme.desc: Hoe werken innoveerders en sporters samen om de strijd op de berg en de halfpipe aan te gaan?

programme.title: The New Frontier S5
programme.desc: Venus was ooit even leefbaar als de aarde nu. Toen gebeurde er iets en werd Venus gehuld in gloeiendhete gifwolken. Er zijn nu plannen om geavanceerde sondes naar het oppervlak van Venus te sturen om uit te zoeken wat er precies met onze evenknie is gebeurd.

programme.title: The New Frontier S5
programme.desc: Het internationale ruimtevaartstation (ISS) is de basis van de internationale ruimtegemeenschap, maar diens dagen zijn geteld. programme.title: The New Frontier S5

programme.title: Anjaana Anjaaani
programme.desc: The film of two strangers, who meet on a bridge intending to commit suicide. After bonding over their shared miseries,they make a pact to live life to the fullest for the next 20 days and explore various adventures together. As they embark on this trip, they begin to develop feelings for each other, leading to a complex and emotional journey. Will they embrace their new-found love or stick to their original plan?

programme.title: Astitva
programme.desc: The movie follows the story of Aditi, a devoted wife, who discovers her husband's infidelity. As she confronts her husband and delves deeper into the truth, she begins to question her own identity and place in society.

programme.title: C Kkompany
programme.desc: A comedy film about three friends who start a fictitious company called C Kkompany to extort money from the corrupt people in their neighborhood. However, their plan backfires when the news of their company spreads like wildfire, and they become the talk of the town. The movie showcases the hilarious consequences of their actions and how they try to redeem themselves in front of the public.

programme.desc: Dive into these timeless tracks that shaped Hindi cinema's musical heritage. The golden touch of B.R. Chopra - where every song became legendary.

programme.desc: The Original Bollywood Divas! Hema's elegance + Parveen's sass = Unbeatable 70s magic. Press play for nostalgia in every note!

programme.title: Dance Hits
programme.desc: Pure nostalgia on the dance floor! Celebrate the vibrant sounds of old-school Hindi dance music with timeless beats and retro charm.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: January 1944 to June 1944. American and British troops are pinned down at Anzio for months, while at Monte Cassino, the killing goes on and on. African-Americans, incensed at the segregation of the armed forces, put pressure on the military to make some changes. In May, allied soldiers at Cassino and Anzio resume their drive northward in Italy, liberating Rome on 4 June, but they let the retreating German army get away. A series by Ken Burns. Part 6 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: 6 June 1944: D-Day. In the early hours of 6 June 1944, the invasion of France begins. A million-and-a-half men take part. It is the bloodiest day in American history since the Civil War, though the Allies succeed in tearing a 45-mile gap in Hitler's vaunted Atlantic Wall. By day's end more than 150,000 men have landed on French soil, and more men, equipment and supplies are coming ashore every hour. A series by Ken Burns. Part 7 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: June 1944 to August 1944. American and British troops in Normandy are bogged down in the hedgerows, while in the Pacific, the marines fight their costliest battle to date on the island of Saipan. Back home, dreaded telegrams from the War Department begin arriving at a rate inconceivable just one year earlier. But by mid-August, the Germans are in full retreat out of France, and on 25 August, after four years of Nazi occupation, Paris is liberated. A series by Ken Burns. Part 8 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Autumn 1944. In September of 1944, with their troops in Europe stalled on the German border having outrun their supply lines, Allied commanders gamble on a risky plan to drop thousands of airborne troops behind enemy lines in Holland. When the mission ends in disaster, it becomes painfully clear that the war in Europe will not end before winter. In the Pacific, on the island of Peleliu, the marines fight one of the most brutal campaigns of the war. A series by Ken Burns. Part 9 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Autumn 1944. In the late autumn of 1944 American soldiers suffer terrible losses when they are ordered into the forbidding and fiercely defended terrain of the Hrtgen Forest and the Vosges Mountains. In the Central Pacific, to the delight of audiences back home, General MacArthur returns to the island of Leyte. But months of bloody fighting lie ahead before the Philippine Islands, and the people imprisoned on them, can be liberated. A series by Ken Burns. Part 10 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Winter 1944 to 1945. The Allies are unprepared for Hitler's counterattack in the Ardennes Forest of Belgium and Luxembourg. It is the biggest battle of the war on the Western Front, fought during the coldest winter in memory. By the time the Battle of the Bulge is over, Hitler's enormous gamble has ended in disaster and the Russians are approaching Berlin. Meanwhile, in the Santo Tomas Camp in the Philippines, thousands of internees await liberation. A series by Ken Burns. Part 11 of 14.

programme.desc: The Rabbids celebrate Halloween with spooky antics and completely ridiculous scares.
